events.title: Bowhunter Education Field Day
events.location: Clark County Shooting Complex Education Center (Room E) 11357 N. Decatur Room E Las Vegas, NV 89131
events.description: Nevada does not require a specific Bowhunting Certificate to hunt archery; however, this class will satisfy states that require a Bowhunting Certificate. You must pass both the online class at Bowhunter-Ed.com and the final Bowhunter Education Class field day in order to complete the Nevada Bowhunter education requirements. STUDENTS MUST BRING THE ONLINE COMPLETION CONFIRMATION WITH THEM TO CLASS! What to Expect at the Final Bowhunter Education Class. The class is 4–6 hours, depending on the number of students attending and will include: a classroom session, outdoor shooting/qualifying with your PERSONAL bow. Blood trailing, demonstrations of tree stand safety, using a rangefinder and survival skills are also covered. Most of the classroom topics will pertain to Nevada-specific regulations. Be sure to have proper clothing for the outdoor sessions and drinks. After attending and passing the Final Bowhunter Education Class field day you will receive your Nevada Bowhunter Education Certificate by email when all student scores are submitted. STUDENTS ARE REQUIRED TO BRING PERSONAL BOWS AND TARGET ARROWS!

events.description: This is an entry level class introducing a shooter to Sporting Clays. Enjoy an invigorating ride through the Clark County’s Sporting Clay’s course. A certified instructor will pick up 3 participants to create a team of 4 in a customized golf cart to compete with others in the class. Participants will choose 5 different stations where they will have five opportunities to hit a variety of aerial targets. Instructors will demonstrate shooting techniques and operating procedures throughout the course. This class has no age limit, no fee, but participants must be able to handle and maneuver a 12- or 20-gauge shotgun. All material and equipment will be provided; no personal firearms will be permitted. All participants must be registered to attend. You will be outside, dress accordingly! Everyone will meet at the public shotgun range to view a 3-minute safety video before heading up to the course. Top shot will receive a certificate!

events.description:
Join the Nevada Department of Wildlife for a unique birdwatching opportunity on the water! This free kayaking program will depart from the shoreline of Lake Mead NRA at the Canoe/ Kayak Beach (between Boulder Beach and the Lake Mead Marina). As a group, we will paddle out to the Boulder Islands to observe shoreline birds, learn about bird behavior, and enjoy the beauty of nature. The total distance for this paddle is approximately 3 miles and will involve a moderate amount of physical activity.
Space is limited – registration is required, and cancellations must be made at least 48 hours in advance.
*Entrance fee/National Park pass is required to enter the park.

Program for ages 14 and over. If under 18 years old, parent or legal guardian must be present.
Some paddling experience is recommended but not necessary. We will provide a brief on-land instructional session prior to paddling.

events.title: Birding Series: Migratory Birds
events.location: Pine Creek Canyon Trailhead Pine Creek Las Vegas, NV 89161
events.description:
Join the Nevada Department of Wildlife for the final flight of our three-part beginner birding series on Saturday, May 9! This program will take place along the Pine Creek Canyon Loop Trail in Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area as a part of the park’s “World Migratory Bird Day” celebration.
We’ll explore why birds migrate while spending the morning birding along the trail, observing and learning about the species that rely on this area during their journeys.  
The hike is approximately 2.5 miles and includes some rocky terrain, so sturdy, comfortable footwear is recommended. The trailhead is about 25 minutes from the park entrance – we recommend arriving at the entrance gate by 7:30 am. Entrance fee or National Park pass is required, but timed entry reservations are not needed before 8 am. 
Whether you’re brand new to birding or more experienced, this program is a great opportunity to connect with fellow bird lovers, learn about bird behavior, and enjoy a beautiful morning outdoors. 

SPACE IS LIMITED, REGISTRATION REQUIRED 
Please bring water, snacks, and sun protection. We will provide binoculars, or you can bring your own. Any questions can be directed to Nia Dippon at nia.dippon@ndow.org.

events.location: Lamoille Canyon Scenic Byway Lamoille Canyon Lamoille, NV 89815
events.description:
Join the NDOW Conservation Education team for a wildlife discovery hike to Island Lake! Along the trail, we’ll explore colorful wildflowers, search for animal tracks, and keep our eyes peeled for any wildlife we may see. At the lake, we’ll take a quick lunch break and soak in the stunning mountain views. And if luck is on our side, we may even catch a glimpse of mountain goats, pikas, or snowcocks enjoying the scenery right alongside us! 
Island Lake is a 3.6 mile out-and back hike with about 955 ft. in elevation gain and a starting elevation of about 8,800 ft. Estimated total hike time is about 2.5 hrs. Please take trail conditions into consideration when registering for this event. Ages 9+ are welcome, with adult supervision. Each participant must register individually. Registration opens June 4.

Once your account is claimed/created, then you can go back out to the main page to search upcoming events by clicking “Programs”. 3. Click “Register Now” for the class you wish to register for. Click “Save Changes”. You will need to repeat step 2 and 3 for each youth that you wish to register.

events.description:
As daylight fades, the Mojave Desert comes alive. Join the Nevada Department of Wildlife for a guided evening hike along the Ash Spring Trail in Calico Basin, where we'll search for the reptiles that emerge as temperatures begin to cool. During this approximately 1.5-mile hike, you'll discover the remarkable adaptations that help these animals thrive, learn about their important role in the desert ecosystem, explore the conservation challenges they face, and gain tips for safely and respectfully observing reptiles in the wild.
SPACE IS LIMITED, REGISTRATION REQUIRED.Ages 12+ The trail is rated as easy with some areas of uneven, rocky terrain. Although the sun will be down, participants should still be prepared for hot weather. Sturdy footwear and plenty of water are strongly recommended.

events.location: Canoe/Kayak Beach 36.04004, -114.78052 Lake Mead Boulder City, NV 89005
events.description:
Clark County Wetlands Park staff event:Join the Nevada Department of Wildlife for a unique birdwatching opportunity on the water! This free kayaking program will depart from the shoreline of Lake Mead NRA at the Canoe/ Kayak Beach (between Boulder Beach and the Lake Mead Marina). As a group, we will paddle out to the Boulder Islands to observe shoreline birds, learn about bird behavior, and enjoy the beauty of nature. The total distance for this paddle is approximately 3 miles and will involve a moderate amount of physical activity.
Space is limited – registration is required, and cancellations must be made at least 48 hours in advance.
*Entrance fee/National Park pass is required to enter the park.

Program for ages 14 and over. If under 18 years old, parent or legal guardian must be present.
Some paddling experience is recommended but not necessary. We will provide a brief on-land instructional session prior to paddling. 
We will provide all equipment – kayaks, life vests, binoculars, bird guides and personal dry bags. If you have your own kayak and plan to bring it, please notify us immediately after registering so we can adjust our equipment needs and participant cap accordingly.

You must know how to swim. Life vests are required for the entire duration on the water. 
This program is subject to cancellation if inclement weather or conditions are forecasted.
Please contact Lauren MacLeod at lauren.macleod@ndow.org with any questions.
